whatIs.title: 1. What is EasyWinGet
whatIs.description: EasyWinGet is a simple, accessible web store that uses the official WinGet (Windows Package Manager) catalog to install applications on Windows 10 and 11.
whatIs.point1: Pick apps visually without memorizing package names.
whatIs.point2: We generate a PowerShell script (.ps1) that installs everything automatically.
whatIs.point3: Free, bilingual (PT/EN), and designed for non-technical users.

downloadRun.title: 2. How to download and run the install script
downloadRun.intro: After building your cart in the store, follow these steps to install your apps:
downloadRun.step1: Open the cart and confirm all desired apps are listed.
downloadRun.step2: Click download script to save the .ps1 file to your computer.
downloadRun.step3: Open the Start menu, type PowerShell, and right-click Windows PowerShell.
downloadRun.step4: Choose Run as administrator — required to install most apps.
downloadRun.step5: Type cd Downloads (or the folder where you saved the file) and press Enter. Then type .\script-name.ps1 and press Enter.

motw.title: 3. How to unblock a downloaded file (Mark-of-the-Web)
motw.intro: Windows marks files downloaded from the internet with a protection called Mark-of-the-Web (MOTW). This can block script execution. Follow these steps to unblock:
motw.step1: Find the .ps1 file in your Downloads folder (or wherever you saved it).
motw.step2: Right-click the file and choose Properties.
motw.step3: On the General tab, scroll to the bottom and check the Unblock box.
motw.step5: Run the script again in PowerShell as administrator.
motw.tip: Tip: to avoid the block entirely, use the Notepad alternative below — files saved locally do not get the web mark.

installWinget.title: 4. How to install WinGet (App Installer)
installWinget.description: WinGet ships with Microsoft's App Installer. If the winget command does not work in PowerShell, install or update App Installer:
installWinget.step1: Open the Microsoft Store using the link below or search for App Installer.
installWinget.step2: Click Get or Update and wait for the installation to finish.
installWinget.storeLinkLabel: Open App Installer in Microsoft Store
installWinget.note: After installing, close and reopen PowerShell. Type winget --version to confirm it is working.

notepad.title: 5. Alternative: copy script to Notepad
notepad.intro: If Windows blocks the downloaded file, you can create the script manually and avoid Mark-of-the-Web:
notepad.step1: In the cart, use the Copy script button to copy the content.
notepad.step2: Open Notepad from the Start menu.
notepad.step4: Go to File → Save As, pick a folder, and save as InstallApps.ps1 (type: All files).
notepad.step5: Run the saved file in PowerShell as administrator — no unblock step needed.

faq.title: 6. Frequently asked questions
faq.q1: Do I need to be a computer administrator?
faq.a1: In most cases, yes. Installing applications on Windows requires administrator permissions. Run PowerShell as administrator before running the script.
faq.a2: The script only installs packages you chose in the store, using Microsoft's official winget command. You can review the content in Advanced mode before downloading.
faq.a3: Yes, as long as WinGet (App Installer) is installed and up to date. Windows 11 includes WinGet by default; on Windows 10 you may need to install it from the Microsoft Store.
faq.q4: What if an app fails to install?
faq.a4: The script continues installing the remaining apps. Check your internet connection, whether the app is available in your region, and disk space. You can try installing the app individually later with winget install PackageName.
